title: Every gate verdict binds what it judged and where: the exact base and candidate, the controller commit, the scenario set and the task's scenario, the host, its toolchain and the runner; and says whether it is about the code or the infrastructure
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs, the module comment (the gate's verdicts: `accepted`, `rejected`, `conflict`, `incompatible` with the head judged alone, `stale`, `no_room`, the gate's own host faults and `cannot_judge`, aborts), `record()` (every integrator record is written there), the judging's `gated` closure and its `task.gated` record (`verdict`, `revision`, `base`, `scenarios`, the extra fields, `flakes`, `probe`, `main_read`), `aborted()`, `capped_host_fault`, `rejection()` and the head's run (`run_gate(&head_base, head)`), the `stale` records, `no_room()`; in crates/spawn-cli/src/gate.rs `judge()`, `judge_seeing_base_check()`, `judge_in()` (the gate's arguments: repo, base, candidate, scenarios and the task's scenario; its stdout), `Verdict`, `GateFailure`, `decide()`; scripts/rsi/gate.sh (you may not edit it): the line `| base cache: toolchain ...` it prints during its setup, before any build; deploy/controller.sh (you may not edit it): it writes `.controller`, the deployed commit, at the root of every controller tree; crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql: `task.gated` in the fold and in `spawn_integrator_record`; `spawn task stages` and `last_gate` in GET /api/missions.

The problem. A gate verdict does not bind what it judged. Today a `task.gated` record names the task, its revision and the base; only an accepted one names the candidate, and no record names the controller whose gate and scenarios ran, the scenario set, the host or its toolchain. On 2026-11-08 a gate runner produced two REJECTED verdicts that were its environment (no cargo registry: "candidate's dependency graph does not resolve offline"; a cargo config naming a rustc-wrapper the machine lacked), and nothing in the record told them from a rejection of the work. The owner's rule (2026-11-09): the validation record binds the exact base and candidate commits, the controller commit, the host, the toolchain, the runner and the scenario, and infrastructure failures stay distinct from code rejections. The comparison milestone M2 (a runner judging the same candidates as the primary; /var/tmp/spawn/sync/design-code-state-v2.md) compares two verdicts only when they judged the same immutable inputs.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. Every `task.gated` record carries `class`: `code` for `accepted`, `rejected`, `conflict` and `incompatible` (statements about the work); `infrastructure` for `aborted`, `host_fault` (every evidence, `cannot_judge` included) and `no_room` (the host could not judge); `superseded` for `stale` (nothing was judged). A future verdict must be given a class when it is added; a record never carries a class outside these three.
2. Every `task.gated` record whose verdict came from a gate run carries `inputs` and `env` for the run the verdict is about (the candidate C's run):
- `inputs` {`base`, `candidate`: exactly the second and third arguments the gate was given (full hashes), `controller`: the first line of `.controller` at the root of the controller whose scenarios the mission judges with (the directory two levels above the mission's gate directory), read just before that gate is started, or null when the file is missing, unreadable, or its first line is not 40 hex digits: never guessed, never remembered from an earlier read, `scenarios_sha256`: the sha256 of the concatenated lines `<sha256 of the file>  <path>\n` (sha256sum's format, two spaces) of every regular file under the mission's gate directory, paths relative to it without a leading "./", sorted bytewise, read just before that gate is started, `scenario`: the file name of the task's own scenario given to the gate as its fifth argument, or null};
- `env` {`host`: the judging host's name (`uname -n`), `toolchain`: the text after `| base cache: toolchain ` on the first such line of that run's output, or null when the run printed none (a gate that ended before its setup), `runner`: null for a gate run on this host (milestone M2 names the runner here)}.
When the head is judged alone too (`incompatible`, and a rejection of a real merge naming `head`), the record also carries `head_inputs`, the same object for the head's run (its base is `head_base`). A record no gate ran for (`stale`, a conflict found before the gate, a `no_room` from the integrator's own room check) carries `env` null and `inputs` with what is known (`base`, `candidate` or null, the rest null).
3. Nothing else changes: the verdicts, the counts (`gate_rejections`, `gate_aborts`, the host-fault and no-room runs), the halts, the backoffs and the landings are decided exactly as today. Records from before this change read as `class`, `inputs` and `env` absent; nothing is rewritten.
4. Visible: `spawn task stages` shows each verdict's `class` and its `inputs` and `env`; GET /api/missions shows the latest verdict's `class`, `inputs` and `env` in `last_gate`.

Add unit tests in integrate.rs and gate.rs: each verdict's class (all eight); `inputs` equal to the gate's arguments; `controller` read per run (a marker changed between two runs of one integrator is seen; a missing or malformed one is null); the scenario-set digest (a file added between two runs changes it; a subdirectory's files count; order is bytewise); `toolchain` null for a run that printed none; `head_inputs` for `incompatible`; `env` null for `stale`. In crates/spawn-postgres/tests/: the fold accepts the new fields and keeps reading records without them.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/035.sh (read it). A real `spawn loop` (no model judge) runs one resident of one gated mission on a fake engine; the mission's gate directory is <ctl>/rsi/scenarios of a controller tree whose `.controller` names a known commit; one long-running `spawn integrate` (started once, never restarted) judges through a recording gate that notes its arguments. Task A: a host fault on the base after the setup (exit 6 with the gate's fact), then an abort before any toolchain line (exit 3), then accepted; it lands. Then `.controller` is removed and a scenario file added, and task B is rejected. It checks: (1) the host fault is `infrastructure` with `inputs` equal to the gate's arguments (base also the source's main), the known controller, the digest computed from the gate directory, scenario null, `env` host `uname -n`, the gate's toolchain line and runner null, gate_rejections unchanged; (2) the abort is `infrastructure` with `env.toolchain` null; (3) the acceptance is `code` with the same binding; (4) task B's rejection is `code` with `inputs.controller` null (not the earlier commit) and the new set's digest (not the old), base the source's main after task A's landing, gate_rejections up by one, and the integrator is the process that judged task A. On the live main (984d059) and the deployed binary it fails at (1) in 11-12 s: "(1) the verdict's class (host_fault): expected [infrastructure], got [absent]". A reference implementation (not to land) passed it five times in 32-37 s, and one that remembered the controller and the digest from its first read failed it at (4).

What it saves. A reviewer reading a rejection sees at once whether the host or the work failed and on which inputs; milestone M2 can compare a runner's verdict with the primary's only on identical `inputs`, and every disagreement names both environments. No verdict changes; on 017's scorecard nothing moves but the record's evidence.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation and any build-time code. The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
